The mercury rule in water quality standards is unusual, yet somewhat logical. It states that levels above 200 parts per trillion (ppt) are not permitted, even though the actual water quality standard is 1.3 ppt. This is because federal standards classify anything below 200 ppt as *de minimis*. What makes it particularly odd is that if levels exceed 200 ppt, there is a requirement to reduce them to 1.3 ppt, but if they are below 200 ppt, they are considered acceptable, even if they exceed 1.3 ppt.

The fact that levels are above 1.3 ppt isn't as surprising as the article implies. Environmental regulations can be complex, but this complexity arises from attempts to balance risk, uncertainty, and economic factors.
